lines.speaker: Thea
lines.text: Lyra’s playing at the taverna by the quay, Captain. Hear her first.

lines.speaker: Thea
lines.text: Welcome to the Gossip Stair, Captain. Every word anyone said hangs on these lines. Now try to find yesterday’s decision.

lines.speaker: Thea
lines.text: Chat works well for questions and talk. But once a session is doing real work, a long thread gets hard to scan.

lines.speaker: Thea
lines.text: A canvas is a shared board in the side panel. You and the agent can both see it, and both change it.

lines.speaker: Thea
lines.text: Say the agent adds plan steps. You uncheck one, or write pause before edits. It carries on from your update, not from a buried sentence.

lines.speaker: Thea
lines.text: So: chat for a quick answer to a short task. A canvas when there’s state to keep in view, steps that repeat, or controls you both use.

lines.speaker: Thea
lines.text: Nikos keeps the desks on the Plaza, up the stair. Mind the washing.

lines.speaker: Thea
lines.text: Up two more flights to the Plaza, Captain. Nikos is by the desks.

lines.speaker: Nikos
lines.text: See Thea on the Washing Square first, Captain.

lines.speaker: Nikos
lines.text: Nikos, Captain. Before any chart goes on a table, look at the four desks at the Plaza’s corners.

lines.speaker: Nikos
lines.text: Plan, Terminal, Browser and Changes. Those panels come with every session. You used them on the way here.

lines.speaker: Nikos
lines.text: A canvas adds one more surface, one that you design for the task. It doesn’t replace the four.

lines.speaker: Nikos
lines.text: Now make ready. Start a session in a new worktree from main, in Interactive mode, with the default agent.

lines.speaker: Nikos
lines.text: In its Terminal tab, install, test and build the Book App. Note the test totals: your canvas will use them as its baseline.

lines.speaker: Nikos
lines.text: The visiting guild has lent us a board. Envoy Calla’s in the Loggia, on the Plaza’s west side.

lines.speaker: Nikos
lines.text: Calla’s in the Loggia, Captain, on the Plaza’s west side.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: Make ready with Nikos at the desks first, Captain.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: Envoy Calla, of the visiting guild. Before you build a board of your own, try one that’s already made.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: Awesome GitHub Copilot is a curated collection of agents, instructions, skills and canvas extensions. Ours is the Repository Issues Kanban.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: It pulls your repository’s issues onto a board that you can triage and track inside a session. It comes in a plugin, as you learned on Sunspire.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: Work round the Loggia, Captain. The guild’s notice first, by the door.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: Select Open in Copilot app, then Allow. And read the name before you select Install.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: Ring the bell: Restart canvas extensions. The app reloads them and picks up the new one.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: The crate says accessibility-kanban. The board’s own name is Repository Issues Kanban. Look for that one.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: Each card you move to Plan starts a new agent run. So move one.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: You moved a card, and the agent moved it again. Two hands on one board, and its state stayed in view.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: Petra will show you how to make your own. She’s on the Draughting Terrace, north of the Plaza.

lines.speaker: Calla
lines.text: Petra’s on the Draughting Terrace, Captain, toward the cliff.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: Try the guild’s board with Calla first, Captain.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: Petra, Captain. Now a board of your own. Start small: a shared checklist.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: Type a slash, select create-canvas, and describe the board you want.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: A proposal field, a checklist, and notes. You and the agent can both update them. It doesn’t run tests or edit the app.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: Work round the terrace, Captain. The easel first.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: Slash, then create-canvas. Then the description of the board.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: Say what the board holds, and what must not happen while it’s being made.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: Now ask the mate to read it back. Does her answer match your marks?

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: Where’s the board kept? Open Changes and look.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: Your hand, then the mate’s, on one slate. And not one file changed in the repository.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: The Great Chart is the same idea with bell pulls. Follow the Kite Walk along the cliff to Doran.

lines.speaker: Petra
lines.text: Along the Kite Walk to the Chart Court, Captain. Doran’s by the Great Chart.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Make your slate with Petra first, Captain.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Doran, chief cartographer. This is the Great Chart: a Feature Workbench for the local inner loop.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: It keeps the proposal, the plan, the work and the evidence tied to one session.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Five stages on the rail: Propose, Plan, Baseline, Implement, Validate. There’s no Approve stage. Approval happens in the Plan tab.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Every button asks the agent to do real work, and records what came back. Building the board can take about ten minutes.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Generated results differ between runs. Check the structure, and repair only the part that’s wrong. Don’t regenerate the whole board.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Now run it. Talk to me again when you’re ready to walk the chart.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Walk the Great Chart’s stations in order, Captain. The quill desk first.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: One field and one button. Paste the proposal, and select Generate plan.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Review the plan in the Plan tab. Don’t let the agent start before you’ve recorded a baseline.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Set the marker on the stage the work is at. A stage is marked only from recorded evidence.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Each bell pull sends a surveyor. Send the first one.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: The surveyor’s back with a slate. Check it against the tool output before you trust it.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Let the agent check the feature in the Browser tab. Then look for yourself.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: All five stages green, and a slate behind every one. That’s a chart I’ll ink.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Warden Iris keeps the Dome. Take the stair from the court’s corner.

lines.speaker: Doran
lines.text: Up the Dome Stair, Captain. Iris is on the terrace.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: Finish at the Great Chart first, Captain. Then climb.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: Warden Iris, Captain. From up here you can see every isle on Doran’s chart. Every mark on it has a measure behind it.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: One trial, then the Seal. Take your time. Nothing here is a trick.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: Again, Captain? The light’s good for an hour yet.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: The Seal of Inkwell is yours. Keep the work where you both can see it, and ink only what the evidence shows.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: Tidewheel Caldera is next, where a tested routine runs by itself. And I’ve one more task, if you’d like it.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: The course’s assignment adds an Assess stage after Propose. It compares the proposal with what the app does now, before any planning.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: Ask for that one change. Then run the workbench through, and come and tell me what you saw.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: Back, Captain? What did your workbench show?

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: Evidence at every stage, from this session. And you knew the next decision without rereading the chat.

lines.speaker: Iris
lines.text: The Dome’s lit, Captain. Sail on when you’re ready.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: Welcome, Captain! Kosta's Model Market. Hire a model that fits the job; bigger ones cost more starfish.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: Pick a job off the board, then hire a model and set the effort dial.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: Copilot Fusion's on offer too. It isn't one model: it picks models and a workflow for each job. And it isn't Autopilot.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: Right-sized! Here's some starfish back.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: Right-sized, and a fair price, Captain.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: Right-sized. A quick look's fine on the model you've got, at its default effort. Bigger ones just cost more.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: High effort for a quick look? The default effort would've done fine.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: A higher Fusion level for a quick look? Standard would've done fine.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: That wasn't enough for this one. Try again with a stronger model or more effort.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: Right-sized! A hard job wants a higher Fusion level: more capable models and deeper reasoning.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: Out of starfish? There are plenty hidden round the isles. Come back when you've found a few.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: The whole board, right-sized! You know your models, Captain.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: Not yet, Captain. Oren on Port Meridian teaches models first. Come back after his lesson.

lines.speaker: Kosta
lines.text: Off up the stair? Your starfish and your jobs go with you. Come back any time.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Tidewheel Caldera, Captain. In through the breach, under the wheel. That’s the Clockwork Lighthouse at the head of the bay.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Last light, Captain! Here the crew learns to save a job once and let it run, after you’ve tested it by hand.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Your tasks are in the top left, and the compass up top shows the way, up the Lamp Stair and along the wall to the Lighthouse.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: And five starfish are hidden around Tidewheel Caldera. Your count’s in the top right.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Captain! A producer doesn’t replay the same drum pattern by hand every night.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: They program it into a sequencer once, and let it run when it’s needed. Hear us play it by hand first.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: The pattern is your saved prompt. Hitting play is the manual trigger. And the producer still checks the mix.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Keeper Agnes is up the first flight, on Gear Square. She’ll show you what’s inside the box.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Agnes is on Gear Square, Captain, up the first flight of the Lamp Stair.

lines.speaker: Agnes
lines.text: Lyra’s on the Bandstand by the quay, Captain. Hear her first.

lines.speaker: Agnes
lines.text: Keeper Agnes, Captain. The tide turns the wheel, and the wheel winds the light. But nothing here runs itself until somebody has tested it by hand.

lines.speaker: Agnes
lines.text: An automation is a saved agent run. Four gears: a trigger, a prompt, tools, and a review path.

lines.speaker: Agnes
lines.text: Start manual, and keep it local. A manual automation runs only when you start it.

lines.speaker: Agnes
lines.text: That way you test the prompt, read the output, and get no surprise runs. Add a schedule only when the results can be trusted.

lines.speaker: Agnes
lines.text: For a first one, pick work you already do more than once. Not one that writes code, posts comments, or merges.

lines.speaker: Agnes
lines.text: Tobin keeps the bounty board, up the second flight. A report needs something to report on.

lines.speaker: Agnes
lines.text: Up the second flight to Bounty Corner, Captain. Tobin’s by the board.

lines.speaker: Tobin
lines.text: See the Keeper on Gear Square first, Captain.

lines.speaker: Tobin
lines.text: Tobin Marsh, Captain. Before you build the report, look at the board. Are there work items on it?

lines.speaker: Tobin
lines.text: Open Pull requests, then Authored by me. You want at least three open ones. If it’s empty, run the setup script.

lines.speaker: Tobin
lines.text: Three slips, and each in whatever state it’s in. That’ll do. Ansel’s in the Wheel Works, up the stair behind me.

lines.speaker: Tobin
lines.text: Up the Works Stair, Captain. Ansel’s in the yard.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: Check the bounty board with Tobin first, Captain.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: Ansel, wheelwright. We’ll build a review readiness report: which pull requests are ready to merge, and what’s blocking the rest.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: The Pull requests view lists them. The report adds the reasons: the checks, the comments, and the next action for each.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: It only reads. The prompt’s last line says so: don’t edit, comment, label, approve, or merge.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: Work round the yard, Captain. The drum first, on the west wall.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: Pin the pattern once. One bounded task, and what it must not do.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: The form starts on Daily. Change the trigger to Manual.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: Run in the cloud stays off. This one runs here, on your own machine.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: The prompt says this repository. So tell it which one, and where to work.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: Don’t just save it. The arrow next to Create, then Create and run.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: Now read the log. Open the run and check what came back.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: It ran when you pulled, and the log shows what it did. That’s a routine I’d trust on the clock.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: Greta keeps the clock. Follow the walk along the wall to her court.

lines.speaker: Ansel
lines.text: Along the Clock Walk, Captain. Greta’s in the court under the Lighthouse.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Run it by hand with Ansel first, Captain. Then we’ll talk about clocks.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Greta Hale, bellmaster. Your report worked by hand. Now it can be waiting for you each morning.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Edit the automation, and change the trigger from Manual to Daily. Then choose the hour.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Mind this: it’s a local automation. It runs only if your computer is awake and the app is running.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Work round the court, Captain. The desk first, on the east wall.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: The day gear. From Manual to Daily.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Turn the ring to a time before your workday starts. The day watch here starts at nine.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: The field takes more than one hour. Clear every hour but yours, and leave the minute at zero.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Save it. Then check the card, and read when it runs next.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Look at the gauge. What must be true at eight tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Morning. Nobody pulled the lever. Look in Recent runs.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: By hand it tells you how things stand now. On the clock it tells you what changed since yesterday, and you needn’t remember to ask.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Old Silas keeps the lamp. Take the walk up to the Lighthouse. And if you’ve a minute, Nerys will show you the bells.

lines.speaker: Greta
lines.text: Up the Light Walk, Captain. Silas is on the terrace.

lines.speaker: Nerys
lines.text: Set the clock with Greta first, Captain. The bells come after.

lines.speaker: Nerys
lines.text: Nerys, Captain. The clock isn’t the only thing that can start a run. Twelve bells, one for each kind of news.

lines.speaker: Nerys
lines.text: An issue, a pull request, a workflow that finishes. Choose the bell that matches the event you want handled.

lines.speaker: Nerys
lines.text: But a bell answers to whoever rings it. Start read-only, keep it to one repository, filter narrowly, and read its runs.

lines.speaker: Nerys
lines.text: See the rock light past the breach? That’s the cloud. It runs when your own machine is asleep, on GitHub’s side, with rules of its own.

lines.speaker: Nerys
lines.text: One more thing. A bottle washed up here with orders in it. Issue text can be written by anybody. Read it before you trust it.

lines.speaker: Nerys
lines.text: Read-only first, Captain. Then one bell at a time.

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: Set the clock with Greta first, Captain. The lamp will wait.

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: Silas Thorne, Captain. I’ve kept this lamp since before the wheel had a name. You’re the last ship I expected, and the one I hoped for.

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: One trial, then the last lever. Take your time.

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: Again, Captain? The tide’s still coming in.

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: The Seal of Tidewheel is yours. Test it by hand, give it only what it needs, and read what it did.

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: That’s every Seal in the isles, Master Captain. I’ve one more task, if you’d like it.

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: The course’s assignment: one manual automation for your own work. A clear name, a manual trigger, one bounded task, and read-only.

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: Run it once, read its history, and revise the prompt. Then come and tell me.

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: Back, Captain? What did your automation do?

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: And you can say why it’s safe to run again. That’s the whole craft.

lines.speaker: Silas
lines.text: The light’s lit, Master Captain. The isles are yours to sail.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Night’s coming on, Captain. Look at the chart. Every isle we sealed has its light.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Anchorage Cay and Port Meridian: setup and orientation. You made the app ready, and learned your way round it.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Thousand-Bough: scoped branches and isolated worktrees, and context used on purpose: prompts, files, issues, and instructions.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Keelhaven: plan, change, and validate. Then issues, pull requests, review comments, and failing checks.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Guildcrest: repository instructions, reusable skills, and read-only custom agents.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Sunspire: MCP servers for documentation, and plugins that supply capabilities.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Inkwell: canvases, for shared state that anyone can inspect.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: And Tidewheel: manual and scheduled automations, used safely.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Captain. Off the port bow. She’s followed us since the fog.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: She took the ships that sailed on a guess. She never wanted the captain who checks.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: One habit stayed the same on every isle: you kept a human in control of quality and delivery.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Human judgment stays in the loop at every major control point: before implementation starts, before a pull request is opened, and before any merge automation is enabled.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Fair winds, Master Captain. Practice on small, real issues first.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Welcome, Captain! Dot's Model Market. Hire a model that fits the job; bigger ones cost more starfish.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Pick a job off the board, then hire a model and set the effort dial.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Copilot Fusion's on offer too. It isn't one model: it picks models and a workflow for each job. And it isn't Autopilot.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Right-sized! Here's some starfish back.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Right-sized, and a fair price, Captain.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Right-sized. A quick look's fine on the model you've got, at its default effort. Bigger ones just cost more.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: High effort for a quick look? The default effort would've done fine.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: A higher Fusion level for a quick look? Standard would've done fine.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: That wasn't enough for this one. Try again with a stronger model or more effort.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Right-sized! A hard job wants a higher Fusion level: more capable models and deeper reasoning.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Out of starfish? There are plenty hidden round the isles. Come back when you've found a few.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: The whole board, right-sized! You know your models, Captain.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Not yet, Captain. Oren on Port Meridian teaches models first. Come back after his lesson.

lines.speaker: Dot
lines.text: Off up the Lamp Stair? Your starfish and your jobs go with you. Come back any time.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Sails off the bow, Captain! The lead ship’s name board says Confident Guess.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: First Take! They never look back at their own work.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Unchecked! Nobody read their checks.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Three habits sank, and the evidence held. Guildcrest lies ahead, Captain.
